analysis.investment_thesis: PNC Infratech appears optically cheap — Earnings Yield ~15.4% (EBIT ₹2,066 Cr / EV ~₹13,434 Cr) — but ROIC of only 13.9% falls below my 20% threshold for a "good" business. Worse, the company has generated negative free cash flow for four consecutive years, meaning reported EBIT is not translating into real cash, which breaks the foundation of the Magic Formula.
key_strengths: Earnings Yield ~15.4% (EBIT ₹2,066 Cr vs EV ~₹13,434 Cr) — passes the 'cheap' screen
Operating margins steady at 17.4% and EBITDA CAGR of 11% over 9 years shows some operating durability
Strong promoter holding at 56% with DII ownership of 24.5% provides governance comfort
key_risks: ROIC of 13.9% is below my 20% threshold — capital allocation is mediocre, not exceptional
Chronic negative OCF: -₹499 Cr (FY22), -₹1,454 Cr (FY23), -₹231 Cr (FY24), -₹56 Cr (FY25) — only 1/5 years positive; EBIT is accounting fiction, not cash
Finance costs surged to ₹852 Cr in FY25 (consuming 41% of EBIT), up from ₹257 Cr in FY16 — debt servicing is devouring shareholder value
red_flags: Revenue fell 22% from ₹8,650 Cr (FY24) to ₹6,769 Cr (FY25) — execution / order-flow concerns
Total debt nearly doubled: ₹4,793 Cr (FY22) → ₹9,364 Cr (FY25) while OCF remains negative — debt is funding operations, not growth
Free cash flow cumulatively destroyed ~₹2,433 Cr over four years; the company is burning cash while booking profits
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the surface, PNC Infratech looks like a Magic Formula candidate: Earnings Yield of ~15.4% (EBIT ₹2,066 Cr / EV ₹13,434 Cr) clears my 12% hurdle, and the stock trades at just 12.7x earnings with P/B below 1x. But the Magic Formula only works when EBIT reflects real economic earnings. Here, four straight years of negative operating cash flow (-₹499 Cr to -₹1,454 Cr) tell a very different story — this is a project-based EPC and HAM contractor where revenue is recognized on accrual while actual government payments lag significantly. The ROIC of 13.9% (EBIT ₹2,066 Cr / Invested Capital ~₹14,846 Cr) is below my 20% floor and has been flat for years, confirming this is a mediocre-quality business, not a compounder.

The balance sheet deterioration is the killer blow. Total debt has gone from ₹4,793 Cr (FY22) to ₹9,364 Cr (FY25) while the company has generated essentially no free cash flow. Finance costs of ₹852 Cr in FY25 — up 3.3x from FY16's ₹257 Cr — now consume 41% of EBIT, compressing true economic earnings far below reported net profit. The revenue decline of 22% in FY25 adds execution risk on top of balance sheet risk. I want businesses that earn high returns on tangible capital and convert earnings to cash — PNC Infratech does neither reliably. Pass.
